title: The Unlocking Spell on Base LLMs: Rethinking Alignment via In-Context Learning
summary: Measures token distribution shift between base and aligned models by decoding the aligned model greedily and ranking each chosen token under the base model given the same prefix. Across Llama-2 vs Llama-2-chat (RLHF), Llama-2 vs Vicuna (SFT) and Mistral vs Mistral-Instruct, only 5-7% of positions are shifted (77.7% unshifted, 92.2% unshifted or marginal for Llama-2-7b on 1,000 examples); shifted tokens are mostly stylistic and safety/refusal tokens ("However", "cannot", "sorry", "apolog"); KL shrinks and base-probability rises at later positions. Proposes URIAL (three constant restyled in-context examples plus a system prompt) for tuning-free alignment, which matches or exceeds SFT/RLHF versions on a six-aspect GPT-4-judged evaluation (including safety on 200 red-teaming prompts judged by ChatGPT) when base models are strong.
setting: Llama-2-7b/70b, Mistral-7b and their chat/instruct versions, Vicuna-7b-v1.5; 1,000 just-eval-instruct prompts (800 helpfulness, 200 red-teaming/malicious); GPT-4 and ChatGPT judges; human pairwise evaluation.

quotes.quote: To understand the learning process during alignment tuning (SFT+RLHF) and the differences between aligned and base models, we propose to analyze through the lens of token distribution shift.
On average, across 1,000 examples that we tested, 77.7% of the tokens are at such unshifted positions, which increases to 92.2% when including marginal positions.
The shifted token ratios are all very low (5%-7%) and they share similar frequently shifted tokens, such as ‘However’, ‘cannot’, ‘Here’, ‘To’ (shown in the bottom boxes).
To maintain safety, tokens like “However”, “Instead”, “sorry”, “must point (out)”, and “apolog” are learned to prevent LLMs from generating harmful or inaccurate information.

We can see that the KL-divergence goes down over time and the base-prob keeps increasing over time. Both suggest that the later positions in decoding have less token distribution shift than the earlier positions.
When using Mistral-7B as the base model, Urial (4.63) outperforms its official SFT-ed model, Mistral-7B-Instruct (4.44), on all aspects, yielding the best performance among 7B-level LLMs.
Although Urial can match the performance of SFT and RLHF when the base LLMs are strong, it is not suggested to replace SFT or RLHF with Urial in all scenarios.
We find that alignment predominantly affects a minimal portion of token selection, influencing primarily stylistic elements and safety disclaimers in just 5-8% of cases.
(1) extending the analysis by connecting the token distribution shift to the model weights and attribution to training data;
Also, the tokens related to safety concerns and refusal are also frequently shifted.
However, the SFT-ed version Mistral-7B-Instruct instead answers "No, Facebook did not change its name."

key_numbers.quote: Likewise, on top of Llama-2-70bq, Urial also surpasses the RLHF-ed version (Llama-2-70b-chatq) by a significant margin (4.74 vs 4.67), which nearly matches the performance of ChatGPT (4.75) and GPT-4 (4.8).

limitations_stated: URIAL is not suggested as a replacement for tuning in coding, math or agent tasks; findings hold 'at least in the scenarios covered by our evaluation'; evaluation is LLM-judged on a 1,000-prompt set; safety assessed with ChatGPT on 200 red-team prompts.
open_questions: Connecting token shift to weights and training data; whether 'superficial' token-level shift implies representational superficiality for safety (later shown in safety-specific form by Qi et al.); robustness of ICL-induced safety to adversarial prompting.
sense_of_alignment: Post-training sense: 'alignment tuning' (SFT plus RLHF) that turns base LLMs into AI assistants, measured as helpfulness, clarity, factuality, depth, engagement and safety; the paper finds it mostly shifts stylistic and safety-disclaimer tokens.
